narrative.overview:
The site is the page a client opens between meetings. The name is large, the photograph is a real person, and the next step is a filled button that reaches him. Cool paper, near-black type, and one grotesque carry the whole thing. Softwire’s clarity and Cursor’s restraint are the craft bar. Their identities are not copied.

The broadsheet was rejected: no masthead, dateline, edition language, column rules, or coral flag. Light is the default, because the scene is a desk in daylight. Dark mode is the same layout with the ink reversed.
keyCharacteristics: One face, Schibsted Grotesk, for the name, the role, and the body
A short ink bar under the name, drawn once
Photographs with a 12px radius and one soft shadow
Records separated by hairlines, never by cards

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Near-black does the reading and the action. Color does not decorate a status.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk sets every word. Weight and size make the hierarchy. There is no second face and no italic.

rules.name: The Page Rule
rules.body: Content sits in min(72rem, calc(100% - 2rem)), widening the side margin from 720px. The header is sticky, 4.25rem, with a hairline under it.

rules.name: The Quiet Lift Rule
rules.body: The page is flat. A shadow appears only under a photograph.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: Controls, fields, and the logo plate use 8px. Photographs use 12px. Nothing is a pill, and nothing is a hard square.

dos: Do keep the biography, employers, dates, keypoints, skills, project descriptions, email, and links as recorded facts.
Do let the name, the photograph, and Get in touch lead the first screen.
Do use one grotesque and one filled button.
donts: Don't rebuild the broadsheet: no masthead, dateline, edition, column rule, or coral flag.
Don't put a kicker above a heading.
Don't turn roles, projects, or skills into equal cards or rainbow icons.
Don't invent a promotion date, a client, or a metric.
